summary: Intermittent p99 latency cliffs during request-accumulation phase causing streaming timeouts
description: Issue summary: Customers (Cloudware Analytics, dedicated account) report intermittent, sharp p99 latency spikes that coincide with the request-accumulation phase just before a batch flush. Impact: Multiple streaming connections receive 504 timeouts and application-level retries, visible as short-duration p99 cliffs (300-800ms above baseline) causing degraded UX and increased token costs. Environment: prod-us-east (us-east-1), serving runtime v2.8.1, request-accumulator enabled with default thresholds. Observed behavior: Spikes typically occur during sustained medium QPS (50-200 RPS) with a higher proportion of short sequences (<40 tokens). Behavior reproduces in customer's dedicated pool and observed in our internal repro harness with similar traffic shape. Expected behavior: Smooth latency tail with no abrupt p99 cliffs during accumulation/flush cycles. Frequency: ~2-6 incidents/day for this customer over last 48 hours. Temporary impact mitigation: throttling a subset of connections reduces cliff frequency but is not acceptable long-term.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use sustained mixed-traffic workload: 60-150 RPS, ~60% short sequences (<40 tokens), 40% medium (40-200). 2) Enable streaming responses and keep-alive connections. 3) Observe p95/p99 on per-tenant tracing or per-route dashboard for 10 minutes. 4) Look for short-lived p99 spikes aligned to request-accumulation flush times.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Accumulator flush jitter aligning with scheduler tick causes short bursts of larger-than-expected flush sizes leading to per-batch serialization peaks.
Hypothesis B: Short-sequence-heavy traffic triggers microbatches that interact poorly with KV-cache warm-up, increasing per-request prep time on some flushes.
Instrumentation added: flush_offset_ms, accumulator_queue_depth, per-connection enqueue_time, kernel_selection_time.
Observed: When scheduler tick aligns with accumulator flush, flush_size spikes by 2-3x relative to running average and kernel_selection_time increases by ~40ms for those flushes.
Repro: Traffic replay with deterministic tick alignment reproduces p99 cliffs in staging. Staggering flush offsets removes cliffs in repro.
Related PR: runtime/pull/4521 introduces staggered-flush-offset config and extra logging.
resolution: Mitigation applied: Canary rollout of staggered-flush-offsets on 10% of serving fleet reduced p99 cliffs by ~70% for affected tenant. Customer notified and canary expanded to 40% per their approval. Next steps: finalize a scheduler-aware accumulation strategy in runtime (engineering work item), add backpressure signal from kernel-selection latency to accumulator, and add automated detection/alerting for aligned-flush patterns. No root-cause patch in prod yet; work in progress.
